stories.headline: Federal judge orders the taxpayer-funded pro-Trump TV ads off the air immediately, including spots set to run Sunday night
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Jennifer Rochon of the Southern District of New York on Sunday ordered the Trump administration to stop airing the government-funded TV ads that portray President Trump favorably, effective immediately. The suit was brought by the watchdog group Common Cause, Robert Hunter, a Democrat running for the Alabama state House, and a New York labor union and its PAC; the DNC filed one of several similar complaints. The administration had told the court Saturday that the Department of Homeland Security, through a vendor, had bought ads only through Sunday, but Rochon said that didn’t make the case moot. She ordered the administration to “cancel or cause to be cancelled” any remaining spots, including those scheduled for Sunday night, and barred it from using DHS money to make, place or air the challenged ads. She found the plaintiffs likely to win on the merits. One of the ads was nearly identical to a 2024 Trump campaign spot. Trump said last week that his super PAC MAGA Inc. would help fund the ads going forward; the White House, DHS, OMB and MAGA Inc. did not immediately comment.

stories.headline: A long-lost 1970 Black Sabbath live session, thought destroyed in a fire, surfaces in full broadcast-quality audio
stories.summary: Three months after their debut album came out, Black Sabbath went to Hilversum in the Netherlands to tape a session for the short-lived Dutch TV show Doebidoe, the forerunner of Top Pop. They played a 40-minute set of blistering, often stretched-out songs from the first record, including a version of “The Wizard” with different lyrics and a rare live “Warning,” and mimed “Evil Woman” for the broadcast. Broadcaster AVRO had said the tapes were destroyed in a fire, and until now the only proof the session survived was a silent 20-second clip of “N.I.B.” that turned up on YouTube in 2013. The full audio has now appeared on an unofficial live album, The Lost 1970 Avro Sessions, from a mysterious German label called Avertigro, a nod to Vertigo and AVRO, pressed in a limited run of 666 copies. The recording is also on YouTube and the Internet Archive, and Louder says it is good enough to deserve a proper release. Three days after the Dutch taping, Sabbath played “Black Sabbath,” “Iron Man” and “N.I.B.” on Germany’s Beat-Club.

stories.headline: Suspect in the Eden Prairie, Minn., homecoming-game shooting is out on bond two days after his arrest, drawing fire from Trump’s team
stories.summary: Adam Abdihakeem Adam, 18, posted bond and walked out of the Hennepin County jail at 7:04 p.m. Saturday, two days after his arrest, according to jail records reviewed by Fox News Digital. Police say he shot two teenagers, ages 18 and 17, outside Eden Prairie High School during its Oct. 2 homecoming football game, forcing the stadium to be evacuated. Charging documents cited by FOX 9 say two cars pulled into a parking lot, a fight involving about 10 people broke out, and the driver of one car got out, opened fire and fled; investigators say Adam was driving his brother’s car and that they tracked his phone before, during and after the shooting, after which he ditched it and changed his number. Records show a $100,000 bail or bond option with no conditions. He faces two felony counts of second-degree assault with a dangerous weapon and one count of second-degree riot while armed, and is due back in court Monday afternoon. Trump’s Rapid Response 47 account blasted the release, saying a “Radical Left judge immediately granted him a no-condition bail,” and pointed to police statements linking the shooting to rival Somali gangs.

stories.headline: Tropical Storm Rachel swamps Southern California beach homes, then soaks Las Vegas and Utah — and forecasters say it’s a preview of a record El Niño
stories.summary: Rachel was downgraded to a post-tropical storm on Sunday after a weekend of flooding and damage in Southern California, and its remnants moved inland across the desert Southwest. Oceanfront homes in Long Beach and Newport Beach were partly submerged when heavy surf broke through sand berms built to hold the water back, and flood warnings stayed up along much of the California coast from San Diego to the San Francisco Bay Area. Rockslides briefly blocked roads as the storm moved northeast, Las Vegas set a daily rainfall record Sunday, and the National Weather Service issued a flood watch for much of Utah, including Salt Lake City, with heavy rain starting Sunday evening. Flash flooding and high surf remain a risk. Forecasters warn Rachel may be just a taste of what’s coming: they expect the strongest El Niño on record this winter, with likely record rainfall, big surf and mudslides into next year. California, under an emergency proclamation from Gov. Gavin Newsom last month, is pre-positioning more than 4 million sandbags, 50,000 feet of portable flood barriers and 400,000 tons of rock for levee repairs.

stories.headline: Study: 19 of 21 new cars tested sent data to third parties, and GM’s apps passed VINs to Meta, Google, Snap and Pinterest
stories.summary: A Northeastern University study tested 21 late-model cars and 30 automaker apps from Consumer Reports’ fleet between October 2024 and August 2025 and found that 19 of the cars sent data to at least one third-party company over Wi-Fi, while 28 of the 30 apps contacted at least one advertising or analytics firm. Seven apps passed identifiers such as VINs, email addresses and precise locations to ad and analytics companies. Four of them were GM’s (myCadillac, myChevrolet, myBuick and myGMC), each sending VINs to 10 companies including Pinterest, Snap, Yahoo, Meta, Google, Microsoft, Adobe and the data broker Acxiom. HondaLink sent VINs and location to Amplitude, and the Lincoln and MyNISSAN apps rounded out the list. Unlike a phone’s ad ID, a VIN can’t be reset, so pairing it with an email lets advertisers follow an owner across apps and sites. Ten of the cars contacted no tracking domains by themselves, but their apps did; the Tesla Model 3 was the reverse, reaching 22 ad and tracking companies from the car itself. The testing predates the FTC’s January order against GM over driver data, and GM says it shares data only with contractually restricted service providers.

stories.headline: Category 4 Hurricane Simon slams Mexico’s Pacific coast with 140 mph winds as Puerto Vallarta braces for the worst around midnight
stories.summary: Hurricane Simon pounded Mexico’s Pacific coast as a Category 4 storm on Sunday, its eye staying just offshore while its strongest winds and rain hit the communities between the Sierra Madre and the ocean. The center was moving parallel to the coast toward the Puerto Vallarta area, where the most damaging winds and rain were expected around midnight and into Monday morning. The U.S. National Hurricane Center says it isn’t clear whether Simon will make landfall, which would let it keep its sustained 140 mph winds. Senior specialist Phillipe Pappin said Cabo Corrientes, the westernmost tip of mainland Mexico at the southern edge of the bay where Puerto Vallarta sits, is the most likely spot for a direct hit, and warned of “catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge.” Forecasters expect 10 to 20 inches of rain in many places and up to 30 inches in parts of Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco, raising the risk of flooding and mudslides. National Guard vehicles patrolled Puerto Vallarta as police with megaphones told joggers and dog walkers to take shelter. Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal towns and began evacuations, and President Claudia Sheinbaum urged people in four states to stay sheltered until officials say the danger has passed.

stories.headline: Sex Pistols singer Frank Carter has a Denver fan thrown out for objecting to a women-only mosh pit, then tells critics to ‘stay home’
stories.summary: At the Sex Pistols’ show at Denver’s Ogden Theatre on Friday night, frontman Frank Carter, the former Gallows singer who now fronts the band in place of John Lydon, cleared the pit before “No Feelings” and declared it ladies-only so women could mosh “without getting an elbow to the face.” A man in the crowd objected that women could already do that, and Carter tore into him from the stage in a profanity-laced exchange that has spread widely on video, then had security eject him and offered to “explain it all to you again” outside. On Saturday Carter doubled down on Instagram, writing that any man offended by a women-only pit is “part of the problem,” that the issue “isn’t up for debate,” and that by “ladies only” he means a “trans inclusionary space.” He also posted a message from someone saying he was the fan’s father, apologizing for his “idiotic son” and thanking Carter. The band makes the same women-only pit request at venues across its current U.S. tour.

stories.headline: Citroën brings back the 2CV as a tiny electric concept it plans to sell in 2028 for about €15,000
stories.summary: Citroën has unveiled an electric concept version of its classic 2CV ahead of this week’s Paris Motor Show and says it intends to have it on sale in 2028 for around €15,000, just under $17,000. The original “Deux Chevaux,” built until 1990, sold millions as a cheap, comfortable car with a soft suspension famously meant to cross a farm field without breaking a basket of eggs. The new one keeps the giant roll-back fabric roof and the tiny footprint (it is actually four inches shorter than the old car), and Citroën is targeting a weight of about 1,000 kg, or roughly 2,205 pounds, which is lighter than a current Mazda MX-5. The styling is boxier, with a taller hood, low wheel arches and roll-down windows instead of the old pop-outs. Citroën hasn’t released power or battery specs yet; Electrek expects it to land between the 8-horsepower Ami and the 113-horsepower C3, and the low arches hint at a city car rather than a farm-road one.

stories.headline: Jets beat the Browns 17-12 in the rain at MetLife as Braelon Allen scores the winner with 3:01 left after a botched Cleveland punt snap
stories.summary: The Jets got their second win of the season Sunday, beating the 3-1 Browns 17-12 on a rainy afternoon at MetLife Stadium. Cleveland took its first lead midway through the fourth quarter on a 29-yard Deshaun Watson bomb to rookie Denzel Boston, but kicker Andre Szmyt missed the extra point, leaving it 12-10. The Browns then seemed to have the game in hand when Carson Schwesinger forced a Geno Smith fumble with 4:13 to go. Instead, a high snap sailed through punter Corey Bojorquez’s hands, Trevin Wallace recovered for the Jets in field-goal range, and Braelon Allen ran 22 yards for the go-ahead touchdown with 3:01 left. The Jets’ first-half touchdown came on a 32-yard Smith pass to Garrett Wilson, and Jason Sanders added a 54-yard field goal early in the fourth. No. 2 overall pick David Bailey had his first three-sack game in the NFL. It was a sloppy, turnover-filled day in the rain: Cleveland linebacker Quincy Williams forced three fumbles, tying a Browns record. Browns rookie receiver KC Concepcion left in the first quarter with a head injury after a high hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick and did not return.

stories.headline: Hours after Trump declared a Russia-Ukraine ‘energy ceasefire,’ Russia hit a Kharkiv power plant, and Russian lawmakers say they never heard of the deal
stories.summary: Ukraine’s Presidential Office says Russia struck Kharkiv’s CHP-5 power plant Sunday evening, after President Trump posted on Truth Social that an “ENERGY CEASEFIRE” between Russia and Ukraine was “effective immediately” and that “both parties have agreed.” “Just now, there was a strike on CHP-5 in Kharkiv — on Kharkiv’s energy infrastructure,” President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said at about 8 p.m. local time. Soon after, a Russian missile hit a grocery store in the Kharkiv suburbs, killing three people and wounding nine, including two children, according to regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. A senior Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent that Kyiv had no information about the truce. Zelenskyy told Axios that if Trump “negotiated it with (Vladimir) Putin, please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready, and we will accept it.” Moscow has not confirmed it either. Igor Ananskikh, first deputy chair of the State Duma’s energy committee, said he knew nothing about it and suggested that “Trump often says things to keep oil prices from rising.” Zelenskyy says Russia made more than 200 strikes on Ukraine’s power system in the past week. Less than an hour before Trump’s post, Zelenskyy told ABC News that a two-month ceasefire arranged by Trump and Putin would let Ukraine prepare for a new presidential election, which martial law currently forbids.

stories.headline: At least 139 migrants dead and 84 missing after an overcrowded boat bound for war-torn Yemen capsized off Djibouti
stories.summary: At least 139 people, including children, died when a boat carrying 305 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti shortly after setting out for Yemen on the night of Oct. 8, the International Organization for Migration said Sunday. At least 84 people are still missing, making it one of the deadliest shipwrecks on the busy and dangerous crossing from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula, which migrants use to reach work in the rich Gulf states. More than 80 people survived, all of them Ethiopian. IOM’s Djibouti chief, Alexandre Coissac, said the boat sank close to shore “mainly because it was overcrowded,” and local authorities were overwhelmed as bodies kept washing up. The official toll counts only bodies buried by the authorities. Survivors buried others themselves, and those will be added once they are verified. “What is terrible is that they were buried with no names, in a common grave, like in a war situation,” Coissac said. Survivors are being treated at IOM’s rescue center in Obock. Tens of thousands of migrants cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait every year, even as fighting escalates in Yemen between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-backed Houthis.

stories.headline: Alvaro Pulido, Alex Saab’s partner in an alleged Maduro-era bribery scheme with a $10 million U.S. bounty on his head, is finally in American custody
stories.summary: Alvaro Pulido, a Colombian-born businessman wanted by the U.S. for years for allegedly bribing top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative government contracts, has been taken into U.S. custody, a Homeland Security Task Force spokesperson said Sunday. The DEA and State Department had offered up to $10 million for information leading to his arrest. Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 in the investigation of his longtime partner, Alex Saab, a onetime ally of ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. Prosecutors say the two set up a network of offshore shell companies to funnel bribes to Maduro allies in return for contracts to import food, medicine and low-cost housing while Venezuelans went hungry. Officials did not say how Pulido came into U.S. hands after an investigation by the DEA, FBI and Homeland Security Investigations. He is due in court in Miami on Tuesday. Saab was deported to the U.S. in May by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who took over after the U.S. military ousted Maduro in January, and last month he pleaded guilty, agreeing to cooperate against Maduro and forfeit $195 million. Caracas has said nothing about Pulido’s arrest.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: last voter registration session before Nov. 3, early voting starts Oct. 19 at the library, and loose-leaf pickup begins Nov. 4
stories.summary: Trumbull’s registrars will hold a statewide voter registration session Friday, the last regular session before the Nov. 3 election, though same-day registration will still be available during early voting and on Election Day (questions: 203-452-5058 or 203-452-5059). Early voting runs Oct. 19 through Nov. 1 at the Trumbull Library from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk’s election warning. On Election Day, Trumbull votes at Daniels Farm, Booth Hill, Tashua, Madison Middle, Frenchtown Road, Middlebrook and Christian Heritage schools. Also this week, the Hillcrest Middle School Building Committee gets updates from its architect and construction manager and reviews invoices, and the Library System Board of Trustees elects officers and discusses the poet laureate program. Public Works says the town’s loose-leaf collection should start Nov. 4 and run until every neighborhood is done, with a daily progress map online. Residents can also ask for bagged-leaf pickup as often as they need during the program.

stories.headline: Dave Lombardo at 40 years of ‘Reign in Blood’: it ‘still gives me the chills,’ and if I go into cardiac arrest, play ‘Angel of Death’
stories.summary: Slayer’s “Reign in Blood” turned 40 this month, and former drummer Dave Lombardo told the Loaded Radio podcast that the album still gets his heart racing. “It still gives me the chills when I listen to that album,” he said. “The palms of your hands get sweaty … your heart rate increases.” He joked: “If I go into cardiac arrest, play ‘Angel Of Death’ or ‘Raining Blood’ … and watch me just pop up.” Asked whether thrash is still close to his heart, Lombardo said he enjoys good thrash but thinks much modern metal has gone “very sterile” since recording software took over, missing the “push and pull” of the old albums that sounded “restless” and “aggressive.” He recalled the band in the studio urging each other on (“Faster?” “Yeah, play it just a little faster”) and summed up the record as “anger, angst, adrenaline — everything.” He also remembered late co-founder and guitarist Jeff Hanneman, who died in 2013, as a funny, self-taught “trailblazer” and an amazing songwriter.

stories.headline: LEGO announces a Star Wars x Marvel ‘Hope Assembles’ crossover contest at NYCC, reviving the rumor of a mash-up ‘Iron Falcon’ set
stories.summary: At New York Comic Con this weekend, LEGO announced a new LEGO Ideas event, “Hope Assembles,” inviting fans to submit designs for LEGO Marvel and Star Wars crossover models that could eventually become real sets. It is named after the Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles crossover comic due in early 2027. Brick Fanatics says the contest puts new weight behind a rumor from August about a set numbered 75481 called Iron Falcon, reportedly being considered as a Star Wars–Marvel crossover. The rumor looked outlandish at the time, until the crossover comic was announced the next day. The Ideas event does not confirm Iron Falcon or any official crossover sets, and the site cautions that no LEGO rumor should be treated as fact until the LEGO Group confirms it. Fans who like a mismatched Millennium Falcon can already buy 75389 The Dark Falcon while they wait.

stories.headline: Philadelphia officer Shane Seiber killed and his partner shot 12 times in a porch ambush; the suspect, a city water worker with past gun arrests, is charged with murder
stories.summary: Philadelphia police officer Shane Seiber, 40, a 10-year veteran, died after being shot three times in an ambush in West Philadelphia early Saturday. His partner, a 33-year-old father of five, was shot 12 times and is hospitalized in stable condition. The officers had been sent to the 100 block of North 52nd Street shortly after 12:20 a.m. for a report of a man with a gun on a porch and were shot soon after stepping onto it. Police say the gunman fled down an alley firing at other officers and was caught after falling out of a tree. Officers recovered two handguns and a shotgun, one of them a handgun taken from a wounded officer. District Attorney Larry Krasner charged Eric Lewis, 35, with murder, homicide of a law enforcement officer, attempted murder of the wounded officer, attempted murder of nine other officers who were shot at, and weapons offenses. Court records show earlier arrests on gun, drug and assault charges between 2013 and 2020, and his union confirmed he worked for the Philadelphia Water Department. Seiber leaves a 7-year-old son and a 3-year-old daughter. Gov. Josh Shapiro ordered flags to half-staff.

stories.headline: Gurman: Apple’s ‘HomeView’ hub ships mid-November in four colors, while the new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini arrive Oct. 30
stories.summary: Two days before Apple’s “Welcome home” event on Tuesday, Oct. 13, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports in his Power On newsletter that the company’s new smart home hub, called HomeView, will ship around mid-November, “at least as of now,” about a month after it is unveiled. The new Apple TV 4K with an A19 chip and the new HomePod mini with an S10 chip will reach customers and stores first, on Friday, Oct. 30. HomeView is meant to be the Siri command center of an Apple home: a display driven mainly by voice, with touch support, powered by an A18 chip. It will come in two versions, a countertop model with a metal speaker base in space gray, silver, starlight and pink, and a wall-mounted model with a flat square base in space gray and silver only. Gurman says it will sound better than the new HomePod mini. It will run a limited set of Apple apps and will have no App Store. The HomeView name first surfaced in a trademark filing by a shell company that MacRumors spotted Friday.

stories.headline: Penguins snap their skid, beating Dallas 2-1 in a shootout behind Silovs as Kindel, Crosby and Rakell score
stories.summary: A night after a shootout loss at Columbus, the Penguins ground out a 2-1 shootout win over the Dallas Stars at home Saturday. It snapped an ugly skid and closed out a stretch of five games in eight days. Arturs Silovs started in goal, with Elmer Soderblom in for Ville Koivunen and Spencer Stastney replacing the injured Trevor van Riemsdyk. A Kris Letang goal in the first was wiped out on a Dallas challenge for a Hendrix Lapierre high stick. Connor Dewar broke the scoreless tie early in the third with his first of the season, a backhand off a Star in front that ended Jake Oettinger’s shutout streak of nearly 190 minutes. Tyler Seguin tied it with 29 seconds left on a deflection with Oettinger pulled. After a scoreless overtime, Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby scored in the shootout, Wyatt Johnston kept Dallas alive, Rickard Rakell went top shelf in Round 4 and Silovs stopped Mikko Rantanen to win it. PensBurgh called it the team’s best all-around effort since the opening-night rout of the Flyers.

stories.headline: Tesla says its Austin Cybercab fleet grew 8x in a month to 300-plus, and names Dallas as the next city
stories.summary: Tesla has given its first official count of its active Cybercab fleet. The Robotaxi account posted Saturday that one month after launch the service had “scaled to 300+ Cybercabs serving Austin – an 8x increase in 30 days.” Tesla AI software chief Ashok Elluswamy added: “Two years since the 10/10 Cybercab WeRobot event, the cabs are everywhere in Austin now. Dallas soon,” the first time Tesla has named the next city for public Cybercab rides. Public rides opened in Austin on Sept. 4. The fleet passed 100 in late September after jumping from 58 to 125 vehicles in a single week, and on Thursday Tesla added 150 Cybercabs to the Texas automated-vehicle registry, raising its registered count from 169 to 319.

stories.headline: Babylon Bee: ‘Heaven Excited To Finally Get Answer To Who Would Win A Fight Between God And Mike Ditka’
stories.summary: The Babylon Bee marks Mike Ditka’s death at 86 by settling the oldest Bears-fan debate. Heaven’s residents gather for the long-awaited “Ditka v. God” showdown. “We know Ditka would win against a hurricane,” one resident explains, and that it would be a tie against a hurricane named ‘Ditka.’ An increasingly exasperated angel tries to explain that the Lord is “the eternal source of all power and existence” and that every ounce of Ditka’s strength comes from Him. The fans reply that this only means a God-strengthened Ditka is unbeatable. The kicker: when Ditka kneels before the Lord in worship, Bears fans take it as a sign he is running out the clock on a victory.
